provenance.source_title: Visual fields, foraging and collision vulnerability in gulls (Laridae)
provenance.methods: ophthalmoscopic reflex technique, measured in 2019 on captured birds
provenance.source_access_scope: published article group-level summary; individual tables described by publisher, not ingested
provenance.sampling_note: Means and standard errors summarize three studied species; individual n below should not be misconstrued as 10 independent behavioral trials

source_qualitative_observation: Birds pitching their heads approximately 50 degrees down in level flight can project dorsal frontal blind region in direction of travel; actual prevalence and collision probability were not measured.
measurement_limitations: Binocular width 35.1 degrees is the maximum at some elevations, not a constant azimuth band over a full sphere
A vertical binocular extent does not specify precise 3D angular boundaries or individual retinal maps
The frontal blind onset is defined for resting head posture in the source reference frame; translating to flight posture requires measured head rotations
Small n (4,3,3), species means only; do not invent held-out birds, trial labels or retinal neural responses
These optical field measurements contain no measured choice-action-reward data and cannot distinguish veridical geometry from Hoffman's adaptive interface theory

rival_hypothesis_sources.role: Hoffman et al. Interface Theory of Perception (2015); theory, not gull behavioral result
Prakash et al. Fitness Beats Truth (2021) within specified mathematical assumptions
Mattes 2026 critical analysis; counter-evidence to universal evolutionary interpretation
